entities.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
entities.anchor: GIST → KIT or PDGFRA; if neither, think SDH or RAS-pathway biology.
snv: Driver — KIT activating SNVs/indels; alternative PDGFRA activating variants (including D842V)
Alternative subsets — SDHA/B/C/D inactivation, NF1 loss, or BRAF activation
rearr: Rare reported subset — NTRK fusions; careful distinction from other GI mesenchymal tumors is essential
other: Alternative SDH-deficiency mechanism — SDHC promoter hypermethylation
entities.pitfall: KIT protein expression is not the same as a KIT mutation. Genotype alone does not determine metastatic risk. SDH/NF1 abnormalities may reflect germline predisposition; a tumor result alone does not establish this.

entities.name: Pleuropulmonary blastoma
entities.anchor: Childhood pleuropulmonary blastoma → two DICER1 hits.
snv: Driver — DICER1 loss-of-function plus an RNase IIIb hotspot missense mutation
Progression/cooperating — TP53 inactivation; RAS-pathway lesions in subsets
cnv: Cooperating — TP53 allelic loss in a subset
entities.pitfall: The loss-of-function DICER1 hit is often germline but may be somatic. Types I–III are combined. Adult-type pulmonary blastoma is a different tumor; regressed type Ir is outside the malignant scope.

entities.name: Primary pulmonary myxoid sarcoma
entities.pitfall: This fusion is shared with other tumors, including GI neuroectodermal tumors and angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma. Location and morphology remain essential.

entities.name: Kaposi sarcoma
other: Viral driver — Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV / HHV8); viral latency and host signaling promote the neoplasm
entities.pitfall: A virally driven vascular neoplasm. No single recurrent human SNV, amplification or fusion is a defining study hallmark. Classic, endemic, epidemic and immunosuppression-associated settings are combined.

entities.name: Malignant gastrointestinal neuroectodermal tumor
aliases: clear cell sarcoma-like tumor of gastrointestinal tract
entities.anchor: GI neuroectodermal tumor → EWSR1 with ATF1 or CREB1.
entities.pitfall: Related fusion families occur in clear cell sarcoma, but this tumor lacks convincing melanocytic differentiation. An EWSR1 break-apart result does not by itself identify the partner or the diagnosis.

entities.name: Epithelioid inflammatory myofibroblastic sarcoma
entities.anchor: Aggressive epithelioid IMT-family tumor → ALK fusion.
rearr: Driver — RANBP2::ALK or RRBP1::ALK; other partners are reported
entities.pitfall: Included for its malignant behavior. Conventional inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor is an intermediate neoplasm and excluded from this atlas. ALK fusion alone does not establish this aggressive phenotype.

entities.name: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of liver
entities.anchor: Embryonal liver sarcoma → C19MC activation plus TP53 damage.
cnv: Cooperating — TP53 copy-number loss in a subset
rearr: Characteristic in molecular series — 19q13 structural rearrangements involving the C19MC microRNA region
entities.pitfall: A recurrent pattern from small molecular cohorts, not a required universal diagnostic criterion. C19MC involvement can also occur in its mesenchymal hamartoma precursor.

entities.name: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, fibrosarcomatous
entities.anchor: Fibrosarcomatous DFSP retains PDGF-ligand fusion biology.
cnv: Progression-associated — increased COL1A1::PDGFB fusion copy number in a subset
rearr: Alternative subset — PDGFD fusions, including EMILIN2::PDGFD
entities.pitfall: Only the malignant fibrosarcomatous form is included. Conventional DFSP is intermediate. The fusion is shared with conventional DFSP and does not itself prove fibrosarcomatous transformation.

entities.name: Pleomorphic dermal sarcoma
entities.anchor: Pleomorphic dermal sarcoma → UV-related tumor-suppressor damage.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, NOTCH1/2, FAT1, CDKN2A and TERT promoter alterations
cnv: Associated — complex gains and losses; no single defining copy-number signature
entities.pitfall: Substantial genetic overlap with atypical fibroxanthoma; depth, necrosis and invasive features distinguish the malignant phenotype. Atypical fibroxanthoma is outside the malignant-only scope.

coverage.basis: Additional cross-system malignant entities checked against primary molecular studies.
merged: PPB histologic types combined; conventional intermediate IMT and DFSP excluded while their aggressive sarcomatous counterparts are included.
excluded: Regressed PPB type Ir and atypical fibroxanthoma.
limitations: GIST genotype is not equivalent to metastatic behavior. The nosology of rare NTRK-fusion GI tumors requires careful pathological review.
